question: do the TFs bound at a distal element, weighted by whether those TFs are causal for the gene in K562 Perturb-seq, predict a CRISPR-validated enhancer-gene link better than distance and better than accessibility?

decision_threshold_stated_before_numbers.rule: all three must hold; failing (i) = no increment, failing (ii) = reads the gene and the distance, failing (iii) = reads TF density not TF identity

ground_truth.source: EP CRISPR benchmark (EngreitzLab/CRISPR_comparison), K562 arm: EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.training_K562.GRCh38.tsv.gz + K562 rows of EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.heldout_5_cell_types.GRCh38.tsv.gz

ladder_gate_applied_to_every_rung.rule: paired per-seed delta >= 0.01 in >= 4/5 partitions -- the SAME bar the question under test is held to, applied to every rung so no rung earns a positive claim on a number that would have failed it

screen_conditioned_ladder.why: six K562 screens with a 14x spread in positive rate; element width sits in the accessibility block and is close to a screen label, so a rung can pay by naming the batch

tf_axis_permutation.what_is_held_fixed: the element, the gene, the EXACT number of bound TFs, and the gene's EXACT z distribution over all profiled TFs (a permuted column is the same multiset, so the GENE block is bit-identical). Only the correspondence between a TF's occupancy and a TF's causality is destroyed.

verdict: NEITHER WHICH TFs NOR HOW MANY -- TF CAUSALITY IS NOT DETECTED OVER AN OCCUPANCY-COUNT BASELINE, AND THE OCCUPANCY COUNT DOES NOT CLEAR THE SAME BAR EITHER. Of the four rungs of the ladder only ACCESSIBILITY clears the threshold this module fixed before seeing any number, and the element's TF set -- counted or weighted by causality -- is sub-threshold both ways. On 11,545 powered distal K562 CRISPR pairs at a 0.0396 positive base rate (457 positives), chromosome-held-out AUPRC is 0.2786 for distance alone (7.0x the base rate), 0.0829 for accessibility alone, 0.0744 for gene responsiveness with no element information at all, 0.3438 for distance + accessibility, 0.3524 once the raw COUNT of the 507 profiled TFs bound at the element is added, and 0.3587 once those TFs are WEIGHTED by their Perturb-seq causality for the gene. One nuisance has to be named before any of that is read as chromatin: the K562 arm is 6 screens whose positive rates run 0.0123 to 0.1801, and the screen one-hot ALONE, with no element and no distance, reaches 0.0590 (1.5x the base rate). Told which screen a pair came from, accessibility still adds +0.0616 (5/5 partitions at the bar) against +0.0652 when it is not, so the accessibility rung is not explained by batch. Read as a ladder: accessibility adds +0.0652 to distance, the raw number of bound TFs adds a further +0.0086, and weighting those TFs by whether their knockdown actually moves the gene adds only +0.0063 on top -- below the prespecified 0.010 bar and clearing it in 2/5 chromosome partitions. Against the two baselines the question named, TF causality does add (+0.0149 over distance+accessibility, +0.0801 over distance alone), but 58% of that increment is bought by counting TFs, which needs no Perturb-seq. The DEGREE-MATCHED element swap says the same thing in the sharpest form available here: on the TF-causality-only arm, which has no distance feature to lose, a decoy element carrying the same NUMBER of bound TFs but a DIFFERENT TF SET scores 0.1036 against the real element's 0.0959 -- 108% of it, with the real element winning 0% of 20 draws -- and the decoy landing slightly ABOVE the real element is NOT read as a reversal; it is what no pair-specific signal looks like, the real TF-identity features being replaced by a smoother draw from the same distribution. THE CLEANER IDENTITY TEST AGREES AND IS THE ONE TO QUOTE, because it never touches the element at all: relabelling the TF axis of the causal matrix -- which holds the element, the gene, the EXACT number of bound TFs and the gene's EXACT z distribution over all 507 TFs fixed, and destroys only which TF's binding goes with which TF's causality -- leaves the TF-causality-only arm at 0.1008 against the real 0.0959 (105% reproduced, real wins 20% of 20 draws) and the full model at 0.3606 against 0.3587 (101%, real wins 45%), under a DEGREE-STRATIFIED permutation in which a TF can only be exchanged for one of similar binding degree and similar causal breadth. AND THE CONTRAST BETWEEN THE TWO PERMUTATIONS IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE NUMBER IN THE MODULE, so it leads rather than sits in a footnote: a FREE relabelling of the TF axis IS beaten by the real data -- the TF-causality-only arm scores 0.0959 against a freely permuted 0.0870, winning 95% of 20 draws, and the post hoc rank arm wins 100% -- so a module that had run only the uniform control would have reported TF IDENTITY AS A REAL EFFECT. The whole of that apparent effect is TF-side DEGREE: how many elements a TF binds and how many genes its knockdown moves. Hold those two deciles fixed and the real assignment of causality to occupancy loses its entire advantage (20% and 25% of draws). That is the finding, not a caveat: promiscuous TFs sit on many elements and move many genes, and that alone reproduces everything the causal weighting appeared to contribute. AND THE COUNT DOES NOT ESCAPE THE SAME BAR. Applying the module's own gate to every rung rather than only to the rung under test: accessibility over distance clears it (+0.0652 paired, 5/5), but the TF COUNT rung does NOT (+0.0086, 2/5) and neither does the TF CAUSALITY rung (+0.0063, 2/5). So the honest reading is not 'identity fails, count works': BOTH TF rungs are sub-threshold, the count differing only in being consistent in sign (5/5 partitions positive against 4/5). AND THE COUNT DOES NOT SURVIVE BEING TOLD WHICH SCREEN THE PAIR CAME FROM: with the screen one-hot already in the model the TF COUNT rung is -0.0050 and positive in only 1/5 partitions, and the TF CAUSALITY rung on top of it -0.0020 in 2/5 -- both NOT DETECTED, and neither is called reversed, because a negative point estimate that no partition supports is an absence of signal and not evidence of the opposite. The screens differ in element geometry (median width 393-884 bp) and by 15x in hit rate, and a wider element carries more ChIP peaks, so the TF count was partly reading the assay. ACCESSIBILITY IS THE ONLY RUNG LEFT STANDING: it clears the bar both naively (+0.0652, 5/5) and with the screen held (+0.0616, 5/5). WHICH transcription factors sit on a distal element, weighted by their causal effect on the gene, is not shown here to matter; and HOW MANY sit on it, which an earlier version of this module credited with the finding, does not clear the bar either and does not survive the screen. The prespecified swap gates (ii) and (iii) both pass on the full model (100% and 100%), but they are lenient by construction -- a decile-matched decoy carries the decile of the distance and not the distance, and the full model has a distance feature to lose. Hold the real distance and swap only the element, and the same degree-matched decoys reproduce 100% of the full model's AUPRC (0.3589 against 0.3587), with the real element winning 45% of 20 draws -- a coin flip. THE DESCRIPTIVE CROSS-CHECK GOES THE SAME WAY ONCE IT IS DEGREE-MATCHED, and this replaces what an earlier version of this module called the one real thing that survived: matched on distance x accessibility deciles only, positives carry 1.70 bound-and-causal TFs against 1.31 (1.30x, p<0.05 in 100% of 20 draws) -- but positives sit at elements carrying 102 bound TFs against 53 for negatives, so that comparison was matched on everything EXCEPT the covariate this module says does the work. Add the n-TFs-bound decile and it falls to 1.71 against 1.42 (1.20x) with p<0.05 in only 60% of 20 draws, short of the 90% bar the module uses for every other matched control. NOTHING IS LEFT STANDING ON THE HEADLINE QUESTION -- not the predictive increment, not the element swap, not the TF-axis permutation, and not the descriptive association once it is matched on TF count. This is a null and the project commits it. The POST HOC detectability probe is reported so the null is not read as stronger than it is: a second, gene-scale-free identity block built from WITHIN-GENE RANKS of |z| moves the full model to 0.3628 (+0.0041 paired, 0/5 partitions at the bar), which is still sub-threshold but says the aggregation choice is not the whole story, and it too is erased by the degree-stratified TF permutation (99% reproduced, real wins 80%).
limits: same cell line on both sides. TF->gene causality is Replogle K562 Perturb-seq and the ground truth is CRISPRi enhancer perturbation in K562. The experiments differ (gene knockdown vs element silencing, different labs and libraries), so this is not scoring a K562 layer on K562 Perturb-seq, but 'which genes move easily in K562' is shared between them. That nuisance is what the gene-responsiveness-only arm (0.0744 AUPRC with NO element information) measures and what the element swap removes. There is no RPE1 enhancer-CRISPR benchmark to escape to.

the benchmark's K562 arm is 6 screens with different libraries, element geometries and hit rates (positive rate 0.0123 to 0.1801). Dataset is NOT a matching key in the element swap, so a decoy can come from a different screen than its target pair. The screen one-hot alone reaches 0.0590 AUPRC with no element information, and element WIDTH -- which sits in the accessibility block -- is close to a screen label ({'Gasperini2019': 500, 'K562_DC_TAP': 499, 'Morris': 760, 'Nasser2021': 520, 'Schraivogel2020': 393, 'Xie': 884} bp median by screen). CONTROL 7 conditions every rung on the screen; the numbers are in screen_conditioned_ladder.

the SCREEN one-hot used in CONTROL 7 is a nuisance covariate available here only because the benchmark records which screen tested which pair. It is not a feature a deployed E-G predictor could use, and it is never part of a biological arm -- it exists to ask which rungs survive knowing the batch, not to raise anyone's AUPRC.

one ChIP file per TF (lowest-accession GRCh38 'conservative IDR thresholded peaks'). A TF whose K562 experiments disagree is represented by one of them, and 12 ChIP-profiled TFs are dropped for having no Replogle perturbation.

507 TFs is a large but not exhaustive slice of the ~1,600 human TFs; an element's real driver may be a TF with no K562 ChIP track, which would make its TF-causality features look empty for a reason that is about ENCODE's coverage and not about the element.
occupancy is binary at ELEMENT_PAD=250 bp around the tested element. Peak strength is discarded, so a marginal peak and a summit-in-the-middle peak count the same.

'causal' is |robust z| >= 5.0 in a pseudobulk knockdown. It is a CONSEQUENCE of removing the TF, direct or not -- bound_causal.py's own finding is that only 31.6% of causal edges are bound at the promoter at all, so most of these weights are downstream effects that happen to be attached to a TF that also sits at this element.

the swap donor pool is the benchmark's own 4,362 elements. That is deliberate (a decoy that is a real tested candidate is a harder control than a random genomic window) but it means the control asks 'is THIS element better than ANOTHER TESTED element', not 'better than random DNA'.

THE PRESPECIFIED SWAP GATES ARE LENIENT, AND THIS WEAKENS THE PART OF THE RESULT THAT PASSED. A decile-matched decoy carries the DECILE of the real distance, not the real distance, so any arm holding a distance feature loses within-decile resolution under the swap and its AUPRC falls for a reason unrelated to the element. Gates (ii) and (iii) pass on the full model largely for that reason. The element-only variants (real distance retained) and the TF-causality-only arm are reported alongside and are the sharper reads; they were added AFTER seeing the first result and are labelled post hoc in the JSON.

the degree-matched swap has 265 pairs per draw (2.3%) whose distance x accessibility x n-TF-bound decile cell held no valid donor; those pairs keep their own element, which biases that control TOWARD the real elements, i.e. makes it conservative.

the causality weights are aggregates over the bound TF set (count, max, mean, top-5, signed mean, and two gene-background-subtracted terms). A per-TF model that learned which INDIVIDUAL TFs matter is not fitted here: with 457 positives over 507 TFs it would be fitting noise, and that is a real ceiling on this design rather than a claim that no such signal exists.

AND THE AGGREGATION IS A WEAKER INSTRUMENT THAN IT LOOKS, WHICH WEAKENS THIS MODULE'S OWN NULL. The bound set is not small: pair-weighted, positives carry 102 of the 507 profiled TFs and negatives 53. A mean of |z| over ~55 of 507 TFs is close to the gene's mean over all of them, so a magnitude aggregate is structurally near-blind to WHICH TFs those are, and a null from it is partly a statement about the aggregation. The POST HOC within-gene-RANK block is included precisely to probe that, and it does move the full model (+0.0041 paired, 0/5 at the bar) -- sub-threshold, but not zero, so 'no identity signal exists' is NOT what this module is entitled to say. What it is entitled to say is that no parameterisation tried here converts identity into ranking power that survives a degree-stratified TF permutation.

the TF-axis permutation (CONTROL 6) preserves each TF's causal vector and each element's occupancy exactly, but a free permutation also breaks the association between a TF's BINDING degree and its CAUSAL breadth, and that association is the entire apparent effect: the real data beats the FREE permutation in 95% of draws on the TF-causality-only arm and the DEGREE-STRATIFIED one in only 20%. A module that ran only the uniform version would have reported a positive. The stratified draws relabel 86% of TFs against 100% for free draws -- with 69 strata over 507 TFs and the smallest holding 2, the stratified control moves less and is therefore the more conservative of the two, which makes the real side's failure to beat it the stronger reading.

the screen-conditioned rungs (CONTROL 7) are themselves a limit on this module's OWN null as well as on its positive claims: conditioning on the screen raises every arm that contains it (distance + screen reaches 0.3179 against 0.2786), so the TF rungs are being asked to add on top of a stronger model than the prespecified ladder used. That is the right test for 'is this batch', but it is a harder test than the prespecified one and the prespecified gates are not rescored on it.

the element-swap donor is drawn uniformly over PAIRS, not over elements, so an element tested against many genes is over-represented among decoys (mean pairs-per-element behind a donor draw is higher than the 2.65 a uniform-over-elements draw would give). That skews decoys toward multiply-tested elements. The TF-axis permutation does not have this defect, which is another reason it is the identity number quoted.
pairs below PowerAtEffectSize25 0.8 are excluded, not counted as negatives, because not-detected is not not-linked. 234 pairs are dropped that way.
AUPRC is pooled over out-of-fold predictions within a seed. Folds are whole chromosomes, so fold sizes are uneven and a single large chromosome carries disproportionate weight in every partition.

a decoy element is required to be on a different chromosome from the gene, which removes the risk that the decoy genuinely regulates the gene but also means the swap changes chromosome-level context (replication timing, compartment) along with the element.

the model is one gradient-boosting configuration, fixed across all arms rather than tuned per arm. A tuned baseline could beat an untuned full model or the reverse; holding it fixed is what makes the arms comparable, and it means no arm is at its ceiling.

VERDICT: NEITHER WHICH TFs NOR HOW MANY -- TF CAUSALITY IS NOT DETECTED OVER AN OCCUPANCY-COUNT BASELINE, AND THE OCCUPANCY COUNT DOES NOT CLEAR THE SAME BAR EITHER. Of the four rungs of the ladder only ACCESSIBILITY clears the threshold this module fixed before seeing any number, and the element's TF set -- counted or weighted by causality -- is sub-threshold both ways. On 11,545 powered distal K562 CRISPR pairs at a 0.0396 positive base rate (457 positives), chromosome-held-out AUPRC is 0.2786 for distance alone (7.0x the base rate), 0.0829 for accessibility alone, 0.0744 for gene responsiveness with no element information at all, 0.3438 for distance + accessibility, 0.3524 once the raw COUNT of the 507 profiled TFs bound at the element is added, and 0.3587 once those TFs are WEIGHTED by their Perturb-seq causality for the gene. One nuisance has to be named before any of that is read as chromatin: the K562 arm is 6 screens whose positive rates run 0.0123 to 0.1801, and the screen one-hot ALONE, with no element and no distance, reaches 0.0590 (1.5x the base rate). Told which screen a pair came from, accessibility still adds +0.0616 (5/5 partitions at the bar) against +0.0652 when it is not, so the accessibility rung is not explained by batch. Read as a ladder: accessibility adds +0.0652 to distance, the raw number of bound TFs adds a further +0.0086, and weighting those TFs by whether their knockdown actually moves the gene adds only +0.0063 on top -- below the prespecified 0.010 bar and clearing it in 2/5 chromosome partitions. Against the two baselines the question named, TF causality does add (+0.0149 over distance+accessibility, +0.0801 over distance alone), but 58% of that increment is bought by counting TFs, which needs no Perturb-seq. The DEGREE-MATCHED element swap says the same thing in the sharpest form available here: on the TF-causality-only arm, which has no distance feature to lose, a decoy element carrying the same NUMBER of bound TFs but a DIFFERENT TF SET scores 0.1036 against the real element's 0.0959 -- 108% of it, with the real element winning 0% of 20 draws -- and the decoy landing slightly ABOVE the real element is NOT read as a reversal; it is what no pair-specific signal looks like, the real TF-identity features being replaced by a smoother draw from the same distribution. THE CLEANER IDENTITY TEST AGREES AND IS THE ONE TO QUOTE, because it never touches the element at all: relabelling the TF axis of the causal matrix -- which holds the element, the gene, the EXACT number of bound TFs and the gene's EXACT z distribution over all 507 TFs fixed, and destroys only which TF's binding goes with which TF's causality -- leaves the TF-causality-only arm at 0.1008 against the real 0.0959 (105% reproduced, real wins 20% of 20 draws) and the full model at 0.3606 against 0.3587 (101%, real wins 45%), under a DEGREE-STRATIFIED permutation in which a TF can only be exchanged for one of similar binding degree and similar causal breadth. AND THE CONTRAST BETWEEN THE TWO PERMUTATIONS IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE NUMBER IN THE MODULE, so it leads rather than sits in a footnote: a FREE relabelling of the TF axis IS beaten by the real data -- the TF-causality-only arm scores 0.0959 against a freely permuted 0.0870, winning 95% of 20 draws, and the post hoc rank arm wins 100% -- so a module that had run only the uniform control would have reported TF IDENTITY AS A REAL EFFECT. The whole of that apparent effect is TF-side DEGREE: how many elements a TF binds and how many genes its knockdown moves. Hold those two deciles fixed and the real assignment of causality to occupancy loses its entire advantage (20% and 25% of draws). That is the finding, not a caveat: promiscuous TFs sit on many elements and move many genes, and that alone reproduces everything the causal weighting appeared to contribute. AND THE COUNT DOES NOT ESCAPE THE SAME BAR. Applying the module's own gate to every rung rather than only to the rung under test: accessibility over distance clears it (+0.0652 paired, 5/5), but the TF COUNT rung does NOT (+0.0086, 2/5) and neither does the TF CAUSALITY rung (+0.0063, 2/5). So the honest reading is not 'identity fails, count works': BOTH TF rungs are sub-threshold, the count differing only in being consistent in sign (5/5 partitions positive against 4/5). AND THE COUNT DOES NOT SURVIVE BEING TOLD WHICH SCREEN THE PAIR CAME FROM: with the screen one-hot already in the model the TF COUNT rung is -0.0050 and positive in only 1/5 partitions, and the TF CAUSALITY rung on top of it -0.0020 in 2/5 -- both NOT DETECTED, and neither is called reversed, because a negative point estimate that no partition supports is an absence of signal and not evidence of the opposite. The screens differ in element geometry (median width 393-884 bp) and by 15x in hit rate, and a wider element carries more ChIP peaks, so the TF count was partly reading the assay. ACCESSIBILITY IS THE ONLY RUNG LEFT STANDING: it clears the bar both naively (+0.0652, 5/5) and with the screen held (+0.0616, 5/5). WHICH transcription factors sit on a distal element, weighted by their causal effect on the gene, is not shown here to matter; and HOW MANY sit on it, which an earlier version of this module credited with the finding, does not clear the bar either and does not survive the screen. The prespecified swap gates (ii) and (iii) both pass on the full model (100% and 100%), but they are lenient by construction -- a decile-matched decoy carries the decile of the distance and not the distance, and the full model has a distance feature to lose. Hold the real distance and swap only the element, and the same degree-matched decoys reproduce 100% of the full model's AUPRC (0.3589 against 0.3587), with the real element winning 45% of 20 draws -- a coin flip. THE DESCRIPTIVE CROSS-CHECK GOES THE SAME WAY ONCE IT IS DEGREE-MATCHED, and this replaces what an earlier version of this module called the one real thing that survived: matched on distance x accessibility deciles only, positives carry 1.70 bound-and-causal TFs against 1.31 (1.30x, p<0.05 in 100% of 20 draws) -- but positives sit at elements carrying 102 bound TFs against 53 for negatives, so that comparison was matched on everything EXCEPT the covariate this module says does the work. Add the n-TFs-bound decile and it falls to 1.71 against 1.42 (1.20x) with p<0.05 in only 60% of 20 draws, short of the 90% bar the module uses for every other matched control. NOTHING IS LEFT STANDING ON THE HEADLINE QUESTION -- not the predictive increment, not the element swap, not the TF-axis permutation, and not the descriptive association once it is matched on TF count. This is a null and the project commits it. The POST HOC detectability probe is reported so the null is not read as stronger than it is: a second, gene-scale-free identity block built from WITHIN-GENE RANKS of |z| moves the full model to 0.3628 (+0.0041 paired, 0/5 partitions at the bar), which is still sub-threshold but says the aggregation choice is not the whole story, and it too is erased by the degree-stratified TF permutation (99% reproduced, real wins 80%).
